name: Dorn
prior: Rangiin (Ahangi, iOS + Android + AUv3, June 2026): real-time physical modelling of sitar, tanpura, sarod, veena with 'accurate emulation of the string-bridge interaction', plucked by touch, tones shaped 'through natural finger movements', free sitar/tanpura, Pro ~10 EUR (VS: kvraudio.com/news/ahangi-releases-rangiin-sitar-synth-for-android-and-ios-auv3-67006, apps.apple.com/app/id6760829177, thebeatcommunity.com 2026/06/03) = a touch-played jawari model on the same phones. Naada Sitar for GeoShred Studio (iOS, $50): physically modelled sitar whose engine 'generates the bridge buzz that creates each tone's overtone halo' (VS: ilio.com/naada-sitar). Mutable Rings string model: negative dispersion = curved bridge, delay length shortened by the half-wave-rectified string output (V: research/src/mi_rings_string.cc:150-186) = sitar-ish buzz as a stock Eurorack feature. SuperCollider 'DWG sitar model' after David Ronan: flat-bridge one-point contact, string shortened by its own output; author: 'sounds more like a banjo than a sitar', 'lacks shimmer' (VS: sccode.org/1-50b, 1-57B). KVR 'Physical Modelling - Sitar' thread: jawari as a ramp, 'can sound like a highly resonant filter being swept' (VS: kvraudio.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=4198277). van Walstijn/Bridges/Mehes DAFx-16 real-time tanpura model (modal expansion, 4th best-paper prize), Bridges/van Walstijn DAFx-17 (tension modulation + distributed bridge contact), ISMA 2014, JSV 2024 (VS: dafx.de, pureadmin.qub.ac.uk). Experimental tanpura repo (modal 80+ modes Stormer-Verlet with jiva / FDTD / waveguide with penalty contact): the bloom comes from a contact point that shifts along a ~4 cm curved bridge, 'pumps energy into higher harmonics over time'; jiva position 'the single most critical parameter'; 'point boundary ... breaks down entirely here'; waveguide 'fastest, but distributed grazing contact is hardest to model this way' (V: research/src/tanpura_README.md). Physical Audio Preparation 2: nonlinear strings with dynamic fret and rattle (VS: musictech.com). Syntheway Sitargen: sitar + tanpura, method unstated (VS: syntheway.net). Not found: a browser implementation, or a jawari string with the thread position as a playing parameter inside a general field instrument with a sequencer and rain. The idea's 'kein Mainstream-Synth hat Jawari' holds for desktop synths and fails for phones.
costNotes: Runtime graph = Saite (BufferSource + lowpass + 2 peaking) measured 0.35 (APP 2081); L3: Saite's double course is measured 1.2 (APP 2082), Dorn's third source (chikari) + gain + pan adds ~0.1 -> 1.3-1.4, not the idea's 1.0. Offline render per string: KS loop with clip + allpass ~30-40 ns/sample -> 254k frames (5.3 s at 48 kHz) ~10 ms in the worker; waveguide with an 8-16-point bridge profile ~3x; 60-80-mode modal with distributed contact ~130 ms (borderline for a phone warm-up of 70 strings). Cache breaks the spec: genKS renders decay*1.05+0.05 s, Nachklang 5 s = 254k frames = 1 MB per string, KS_CACHE caps at 80 entries / 1e7 frames = 39 such strings (APP 4663-4672); 5 Faden steps x 14 notes = 70 strings = 17.8M frames -> warm-up evicts itself; with MIDI (37 keys x 5) hopeless. Mitigations: 3 steps, warm the current step only, 24 kHz internal render, Nachklang default <= 3.5 s. Nearest-string fallback retunes within +-2 octaves by rate (APP 4675-4685): for a nonlinear string this scales the bloom's time 0.25-4x -> limit Dorn to +-4 semitones. Worklet alternative (R: webaudio.md section 4/10): waveguide 0.24 + 3 k-rate params 0.09 + contact 0.03 + native body 0.09 = ~0.45 per voice (L3 ~0.75 with 2 strings + chikari in one node): live thread while ringing, meend glides via freq, tilt while ringing, no cache, no warm-up; native live KS is impossible (feedback < 128 frames, R section 7). Recommended path: worklet live, offline as the no-worklet fallback.
soundHeld: Not held: struck-only by spec, like Saite (no setF glide, no live Hoehe after the pluck; Bebung works through BufferSource.detune as in Saite, APP 3715). The spec's one-point clip (y' = y < h ? y : h + (y-h)*r at one loop point) is the Ronan/sccode model class whose author reports 'banjo, no shimmer': it yields a step (buzz while amplitude > h, clean KS after) rather than the tanpura bloom, which needs a grazing contact whose point moves with amplitude (distributed curved bridge + thread bump, or at least Rings' rectified-displacement delay modulation). Offline, a two-delay-line waveguide with an 8-16-point bridge profile is affordable and is the fix. Acceptance test: the spectrogram of one 5 s note shows a high-harmonic ridge that moves over 1-3 s, and the thread step shifts where it starts.
soundBurst: Puls: every hit rings its full Nachklang (o.decayMul is read by all struck engines, APP 3608-4535, but no caller sets it - grep finds no setter - so lanes cannot shorten it today); 5 s x 5.6 hits/s (1/16 at 84 bpm, gate 0.9*step, APP 5967/5980) = 28 live voices ~10 of the 14 mobile units (APP 2084), Saite at 3 s costs 6. The bloom needs >= 1-2 s, so 1/8 and 1/16 lanes hear only a buzzy Saite; Dorn in Puls is a slow-lane drone instrument (as the idea says) and needs a Nachklang cap. Sporenregen: fine as a sixth RG_S strike (precedent 'sai', APP 8772) if the warm-up covers the field's notes for the current Faden step.
failureModes: One-point clip != bloom: step from buzz to clean instead of a travelling formant; needs distributed curved contact (waveguide + bridge profile + thread bump, offline-affordable) or Rings-style amplitude-driven delay modulation; spectrogram acceptance test
Cache x5 overflows KS_CACHE (1e7 frames = 39 strings of 5.3 s) for 5 steps x 14 notes; warm-up thrashes; MIDI impossible -> 3 steps, current-step warm-up, 24 kHz render, Nachklang <= 3.5 s
Nearest-string rate fallback up to +-2 octaves scales the bloom 0.25-4x -> audibly a different instrument on the first note of a degree; limit to +-4 semitones
Puls budget: 5 s Nachklang x fast lane = ~10 units; bloom inaudible on fast lanes -> buzzy Saite; cap Nachklang / lane voices
Hoehe frozen at the pluck: Gestik tilt changes nothing while the note rings, unlike every held engine; the live worklet variant (~0.45) removes this and adds meend glides
Collapses into Saite when amplitude never exceeds the thread height (low velocity, low Faden): defaults must make the first note sirr (Faden 0.5, Kruemmung 0.5, vel >= 0.4)
Chikari octave strings per voice at L3 x 4 fingers = mush; chikari only for Puls/slow use or default off
Phone speakers: collision energy at 2-8 kHz dominates while the fundamental is weak -> thin rattle; high shelf or higher Koerper default
L3 cost 1.3-1.4, not 1.0 (Saite's measured double course is already 1.2)
verdict: Rare, not new: Rangiin (June 2026) plays real-time jawari models of sitar and tanpura by touch on the same phones Myzel targets, GeoShred's Naada Sitar does it on iPad, and the curved-bridge trick is a stock Rings feature; what Dorn adds is the thread position as a playing parameter inside a field instrument with Puls and Sporenregen. Feasible as an offline-rendered Saite sibling (native runtime, 0.35 units; L3 about 1.3-1.4, not 1.0), but the spec's one-point clip is the model whose own author called it 'banjo, no shimmer' - the bloom needs the distributed curved contact or at least amplitude-driven delay modulation - and 5 Faden steps x 5 s strings x a two-octave scale overflow the 1e7-frame KS cache. The better instrument is the live worklet variant (about 0.45 units: live thread while ringing, meend glides, no cache or warm-up) with offline as the no-worklet fallback; as a Puls hit it shows the bloom only on slow lanes, and fast lanes get a buzzy Saite at about 10 budget units unless Nachklang is capped.
